title: Xanthe and the Verdict
premise: Emrys Voss, an insurance investigator with a flawless photographic memory, is hired by a nervous stranger who pays triple to prove that a murder scheduled for the night of the solstice will never happen — a murder no one has reported, in a town where everyone insists the intended victim died years ago. As Emrys digs into the case of Larkspur Hollow's beloved matriarch, Odette Crane, he discovers the 'dead' woman is alive, hidden by neighbors protecting her from a verdict she already lost once. The real target is the witness who can overturn it: Odette herself, whose testimony once condemned an innocent man. Emrys must choose between closing the file and saving her, and in the end he burns his own perfect record — and his memory of the client's face — to keep her safe.
about_author: Zephyrine Montrose is the pen name of a former court stenographer who spent fifteen years transcribing verdicts before deciding to write the stories transcripts couldn't hold. They live in a coastal town much like Larkspur Hollow, where the fog keeps everyone's secrets.

chapters.title: Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: POV Emrys Voss. A gray-eyed stranger hires Emrys to prevent a murder that hasn't happened yet, paying in cash and refusing to name the victim. Emrys, who never forgets a face, realizes with unease that he cannot recall the client's. Emotional beat: professional pride curdling into first doubt.

chapters.title: The Town That Remembers Wrong
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. In Larkspur Hollow, every resident repeats the same story: Odette Crane died seven years ago, drowned. But the dates on the gravestone don't match the weather records Emrys memorized. Emotional beat: the uncanny friction between his perfect memory and a town's rehearsed forgetting.

chapters.title: A House Kept Warm
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. He stakes out the shuttered Crane house and finds fresh bread steam on a window, a light moving behind boarded glass. Someone is living there. Emotional beat: quiet thrill of discovery shadowed by the sense of being watched back.

chapters.title: What the Drowned Woman Saw
chapters.summary: POV Odette Crane. Hidden for seven years, Odette recounts the trial that convicted Tomas Reyes of her murder — a murder she survived and chose not to stop. She stayed silent to protect her son. Emotional beat: guilt as a room she's furnished and lived in.

chapters.title: The Client's Face
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Cross-referencing old trial photos, Emrys matches the unmemorable stranger to the prosecutor who won Odette's conviction — now up for a judgeship, with a confirmation hearing after the solstice. Emotional beat: cold clarity; the case was never about insurance.

chapters.title: Solstice Eve
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. The prosecutor arrives in town with two men; the neighbors who hid Odette begin panicking and one disappears. Emrys finds the missing neighbor's boat adrift. Emotional beat: dread tightening as the fiction of the town starts cracking under pressure.

chapters.title: Verdict, Reversed
chapters.summary: POV Odette. Odette decides to end her hiding and testify at Reyes's appeal hearing, even if it destroys her son's fragile life. She writes her statement through the night. Emotional beat: love against duty — motherhood versus justice, finally chosen.

chapters.title: The Long Night of Larkspur Hollow
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Climax: the prosecutor's men come for Odette at the hearing; Emrys uses his photographic recall to dismantle their alibis detail by detail before the packed courtroom, while the gray-eyed client watches from the gallery. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into certainty.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Reyes walks free; the prosecutor is arrested; but Odette's son refuses to forgive her seven silent years, and the town turns its shame on everyone. Emrys realizes his client paid him to be a witness, not a savior. Emotional beat: victory that costs more than defeat.

chapters.title: What Emrys Chose to Forget
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Closing the file, Emrys deliberately lets the client's face blur — the only thing his memory has ever released — and mails the advance to Reyes's defense fund. On the train out, Odette waves from the platform. Emotional beat: peace purchased by surrendering perfection.
